Scoping Consultation
content:
Decision:
 
1.   Agree the new Guildford
Local Plan Scoping Consultation document as set out in Appendix 1
and for the consultation to be undertaken for a period of six weeks
starting in September 2026.; and
2.   Delegate authority to the
Joint Director of Planning, in consultation with the Lead
Councillor for Planning, to make such minor alterations to the new
Guildford Local Plan Scoping Consultation document to improve the
clarity and/or accuracy as necessary.
 
Reason(s):
 
1.      
This recommendation enables the Council to undertake
the scoping consultation under Regulation 20 of the Town and
Country Planning (Local Planning) (England) Regulations 2026 which
is required to be completed before it can formally commence
preparation of the new Guildford Local Plan.
2.      
This recommendation enables minor changes to the
document to improve clarity or accuracy in an efficient
manner.
 
Other options considered and
rejected by the Executive:
 
Option 2: Delaying the scoping
consultation / pausing the plan preparation process (not
recommended). This would lead to a delay in the preparation of the
Guildford Local Plan because the stages of preparation must be
carried out sequentially. Any lengthy delay will risk the Council
not meeting the legal requirement for the Council to publish the
Gateway 1 self-assessment by 30 April 2027 at the latest, as
explained in paragraph 8.4 of this report. Any delay would mean
that the Council would not meet the earlier deadline of 31 October
2026 required as part of the receipt of Local Plan Implementation
Funding (see paragraph 8.6 of this report). Not having an
up-to-date new local plan means that the Borough will remain
vulnerable to speculative applications and appeals for development.
An up-to-date local plan is the only way that the Council can
provide a positive place-shaping role with a coherent approach to
growth that is supported by the necessary
infrastructure.
 
Details of any conflict of
interest declared by the Leader or lead councillors and any
dispensation granted:
None.

Decision:
 
That the Executive approves the
grant of a new 10-year lease at less than best consideration, being
a peppercorn, to Guildford Action for Community Care at Beverley
Hall Community Centre, Haydon Place, Guildford.
 
Reason(s):
 
1.      
To ensure Beverley Hall Community Centre remains
open and available to the community.
2.      
To support the activities of Guildford Action for
Community Care.
 
Other options considered and
rejected by the Executive:
 
1.      
To not agree the grant of a new 10-year lease at a
peppercorn rent, which would not be recommended as this would stop
the operation of the community centre as well as the services
provided by GACC.
2.      
To charge GACC a market rent for a new 10-year
lease; however, this is not recommended, as this would not be
accepted by GACC who operate the community centre on the
Council’s behalf and differs from their current
arrangement.
3.      
For the Council to operate the Community Centre on
its own account; however, this has a substantially higher operating
costs for the Council and would result in the loss of vital
services that GACC provide.
 
Details of any conflict of
interest declared by the Leader or lead councillors and any
dispensation granted:
 
None.

content:
Decision:
 
To approve the award of the
Domestic Gas Servicing & Repairs Contract to TSG Building
Services PLC for a period of five years at a total contract value
of £5,991,263.
 
Reason(s):
 
1.      
The Council has a statutory responsibility to ensure
domestic gas installations within its housing stock are safely
serviced, inspected and maintained.
2.      
A compliant competitive procurement process has
identified TSG Building Services PLC as the Most Advantageous
Tenderer, providing the strongest combination of quality, price and
social value.
3.      
Awarding the contract will secure continuity of
service, provide value for money, achieve savings against the
approved budget and support the delivery of wider social value
commitments.
 
Other options considered and
rejected by the Executive:
 
Option 1 – Do nothing.
This option is not recommended. The Council could decide not to
award the contract and consider alternative arrangements for
delivering domestic gas servicing and repair services. This option
is not recommended as it would create a risk to statutory
compliance, resident safety and continuity of service. It could
also result in additional costs associated with interim
arrangements, further procurement activity and the loss of the
value for money and social value benefits identified through the
completed procurement process.
 
Details of any conflict of
interest declared by the Leader or lead councillors and any
dispensation granted:
 
None.

content:
Decision:
 
To approve the award of the Hot
Jet Washing Services contract to CTG Enterprises Ltd for an initial
period of three years, with the option to extend for two further
periods of twelve months each, at a total contract value of
£334,725.
 
Reason(s):
 
1.      
The Council requires a specialist contractor to
deliver planned hot jet washing services across a range of public
realm assets to maintain safe, clean and welcoming public spaces
for residents and visitors.
2.      
The procurement was undertaken using the Open
Procedure in accordance with the Public Contracts Regulations 2015.
Eight compliant tenders were received and evaluated in accordance
with the published award criteria. CTG Enterprises Ltd submitted
the Most Economically Advantageous Tender, offering the optimum
balance of quality and price.
3.      
CTG Enterprises Ltd demonstrated a clear
understanding of the Council's operational requirements and, as the
incumbent contractor, possesses detailed knowledge of the Council's
sites and service requirements. This will support a seamless
transition into the new contract, minimise mobilisation risks and
ensure continuity of service delivery.
 
Other options considered and
rejected by the Executive:
 
Do nothing - Failure to award
the contract would result in deterioration of public realm assets,
increased health and safety risks and a reduction in the quality
and appearance of public spaces. This option is not
recommended.
 
Details of any conflict of
interest declared by the Leader or lead councillors and any
dispensation granted:
 
None.

To set out a strategy for the
vehicle replacement programme for the 2026-2028 period that ensures
a compliant and efficient fleet to deliver the council’s main
frontline services and environmental objectives.
 
Other options considered and
rejected by the Executive:

Do something: approve the Fleet Programme but
increase the replacement time period. This is not recommended as
this will impact the reliability of the Council’s current
fleet, increase short term hire and repairs costs and prolong the
current adverse impacts on service delivery.

replacing as needed individually. This is not recommended as the
lack of a fleet replacement procurement strategy would result in
poor product support post purchase which will impact on service
delivery and not gain best value for money for the
Council.

Do nothing: No programme will result in continued
increases in repair and replacement vehicle short term hire costs
and would impact severely on the Council’s service
delivery.

dispensation granted:

reversionary lease to Heartwood Inns Limited at 2-4 South Hill,
Guildford on the terms set out in Appendix 1, subject to the
specific consent of the West Surrey Shadow Executive should this be
required.

The tenant holds a protected
lease agreement with a term due to expire in April 2035. While
protected the tenant is entitled to a new lease at the end of their
current agreement, subject to no valid grounds for repossession.
The grant of a reversionary lease removes the uncertainty at the
end of the current term by securing the terms now and the Council
income for a further 15 years.
 
Other options considered and
rejected by the Executive:
 
To refuse the grant of a
reversionary lease may leave the council exposed come April 2035 to
the premises being returned and associated void costs.

purpose:
Approval to adopt Memorial Safety
Policy
content:
Decision:
 
To adopt the Memorial Safety
Policy, as set out in Appendix 1 to the report.
 
Reason(s):
 
The Council has a statutory
obligation to test the safety of and, where required, carry out
works to make safe memorials within its closed churchyards and
cemeteries. It is the expectation of the Health and Safety
Executive (HSE) that burial authorities have a memorial safety
policy outlining their safety programmes in order to demonstrate
compliance with memorial safety legislation. The HSE has
enforcement responsibility for all cemeteries apart from those
located in (closed) churchyards for which the local authority has
enforcement responsibility
 
Other options considered and
rejected by the Executive:
 
The Executive does nothing; it
does not adopt the policy. It is the expectation of the HSE that
burial authorities have a rolling safety programme and definitive
policy in place to demonstrate compliance regarding memorial safety
obligations. If the organisation does not have an approved policy
in place, it cannot demonstrate compliance and leaves itself open
to significant financial, legal and reputational risk should an
injury or fatality occur.
 
Details of any conflict of
interest declared by the Leader or lead councillors and any
dispensation granted:
 
None.
topline: The Executive has decided to adopt the Memorial Safety Policy to ensure compliance with safety regulations for memorials in closed churchyards and cemeteries.

Decision:
 
1.   Note the information shared
in the accompanying ‘Electric Theatre Options
Appraisal’ report from independent experts Blue Horizon
Ventures;
2.   Agree that the hybrid/
cultural operating model is the most appropriate operating model
for The Electric Theatre;
3.   Authorise the Joint
Strategic Director of Finance and Resources to undertake a
compliant procurement process for a new operator of The Electric
Theatre; and
4.   Agree a supplementary
estimate of £50,000 for an industry expert to support the
procurement process for a new operator for The Electric
Theatre.
 
Reason(s):
 
1.    
To update the Executive on progress made to date in
relation to The Electric Theatre.
2.    
Consistent with the Council’s Best Value Duty,
to establish the feasibility and viability of potential operating
models for the theatre, including its use as a cultural and
community arts venue, alongside alternative commercial
options.
3.    
To enable the timely progression of this work in a
structured and transparent way, with regard to stakeholder interest
and the need to maintain confidence in the process.
4.    
To progress with the procurement of a new operator
for The Electric Theatre.
 
Other options considered and
rejected by the Executive:
 
Option 1 (not recommended): in
noting the report from BHV, do nothing, leaving The Electric
Theatre vacant and unused.
 
Details of any conflict of
interest declared by the Leader or lead councillors and any
dispensation granted:
 
None.
topline: The Executive has decided to proceed with selecting a new operator for The Electric Theatre and implementing a hybrid/cultural operating model.

content:
Decision:
 
1.   Note the contents of the
Clean Air Zone Feasibility study report, its conclusions and
recommendations;
2.   To report the findings in
full to the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs
(Defra);
3.   To pursue the recommended
option of working in partnership with Surrey County Council (SCC)
and or any devolved representative authority;
4.   To revise the draft Air
Quality Action Plan, dated August 2022, to reflect the outcomes of
the economic feasibility study following engagement and discussion
with SCC on the shortlisted actions/measures; and
5.   To report back on the
revised draft Air Quality Action Plan within six months.
 
Reason(s):
 
1. 
The studies carried out by Buro Happold consultants
on the Economic Feasibility of a Clean Air Zone are part of the Air
Quality Action Plan for Guildford Town Centre and Shalford Air
Quality Management Areas.
2. 
The details of both reports will be presented at the
Overview and Scrutiny Committee by the author Professor Margarethe
Theseira with officers in attendance.
3. 
To ensure the Council meets its statutory duties in
relation to air quality and the submission of Air Quality Annual
Status Reports under the Environment Act 1995.
4. 
The report aims to provide the Committee with an
update on progress of air quality projects and other statutory air
quality priorities in fulfilment of Part IV of the Environment Act
1995 Local Air Quality Management, as amended by the Environment
Act 2021.
5. 
Whilst the study is a large part of the Air Quality
Action Plan for Guildford Town Centre, the final plan requires some
additional air quality assessments which the original consultants
Air Pollution Services Ltd have been earmarked to complete in the
financial year 2026/27. This was delayed due to the lack of funding
available in 2025/26.
 
Other options considered and
rejected by the Executive:
 
Option 2: Pursue the Clean Air
Zone concept by requesting that Surrey County Council formally
assess the viability, under their Transport Act 2000
powers.
 
Details of any conflict of
interest declared by the Leader or lead councillors and any
dispensation granted:
 
None.
topline: The Executive has decided to approve recommendations from a Clean Air Zone Feasibility study report for the Air Quality Action Plan in Guildford Town Centre and Shalford.

purpose: To review the lease terms.
content:
Decision:
 
To agree to vary the terms of
the existing lease to Stonegate Pub Company Limited over 2-3 Armour
Buildings, Bridge Street, Guildford on the terms set out in Exempt
Appendix 1.
 
Reason(s):
 
1.      
An agreement to the amended terms provides the
Council with certainty of rental income to lease expiry in
September 2030 and continuity of the repair liability as provided
in the current lease which is to be transferred to the new lease.
The benefits of such certainty outweigh the significant financial
exposure and risk that an immediate surrender of the lease, or
refusal to agree to the amended terms present.
2.      
As part of the Group’s ongoing restructure,
Stonegate UK Midco Limited (a newly incorporated company) will be
placed as the ultimate parent company and will act as guarantor for
the leases. In that position, it sits at the top of the structure
and has control of the wider Stonegate Group, including the
operating businesses. From a landlord perspective, this offers a
more secure group structure and introduces a UK based guarantor,
which is more straightforward from an enforcement perspective and
sits directly above the businesses responsible for the
leases.
 
Other options considered and
rejected by the Executive:
 
Option 2 – to accept an
immediate surrender of the current lease in return for the payment
of a sum to the Council equivalent to 6 months' rent. Such
consensual agreement must be concluded by 24th June
2026.
 
Option 3 – to refuse the
varied lease terms. In this situation, the tenant’s
restructuring adviser has indicated that such leases will not
transfer to the new group structure, will remain at risk and may be
subject to a more formal restructure process. Landlords should not
expect the tenant’s lease obligations to continue to be
funded. It is not clear at this point what path this would take but
it is likely that once the restructuring exercise has completed,
the balance of any leases remaining in Stonegate Pub Company Ltd
may be resolved either in CVA or restructure plan via court order.
Officers are advised that the debt is substantial including a
substantial private equity secured debt which would come before
landlord’s debt.
 
Details of any conflict of
interest declared by the Leader or lead councillors and any
dispensation granted:
 
None.
topline: The Executive has decided to approve the recommendations to vary the terms of the lease to Stonegate Pub Company Limited.

purpose:
Agree local plan timetable and notice of
intention to commence local plan preparation
content:
Decision:
1.    
Agree the ‘Guildford Local Plan
timetable’ and the ‘statement that the timetable is to
have effect’ as set out respectively in Appendices 1 and 2 to
this report and that they be published on 5 June 2026 or as soon as
is reasonably practicable thereafter;
2.    
agree the ‘notice of intention to commence
local plan preparation’ as set out in Appendix 3 to this
report and that it is made available on 5 June 2026 or as soon as
is reasonably practicable thereafter;
3.    
delegate authority to the Joint Assistant Director:
Planning, in consultation with the Lead Councillor for Planning, to
make such minor alterations to the documents referred to in
paragraphs 2.1.1 and 2.1.2 above to improve their clarity, accuracy
and/or format as she may deem necessary; and
4.    
delegate authority to the Joint Assistant Director:
Planning in consultation with the Lead Councillor for Planning to
update, revise and publish the ‘Guildford Local Plan
timetable’ following 5 June 2026 in accordance with the
relevant legislative requirements.
 
Reason(s):
 
1.    
This recommendation enables the Council to set out
its timetable for preparing the Guildford Local Plan under
Government’s new plan-making system. It will provide clarity
to all stakeholders regarding the timing of key stages in the
Guildford Local Plan preparation process. It will fulfil the
statutory requirements regarding local plan timetables1 including
regarding their form and content.
2.    
This recommendation enables the Council to progress
with preparation of the Guildford Local Plan under
Government’s new plan-making system. It will also fulfil the
statutory requirement regarding preparing and making available a
‘notice of intention to commence local plan
preparation’2.
3.    
This recommendation enables minor changes to the
documents to improve clarity or accuracy in an efficient manner
alongside ensuring that the format of the Local Plan timetable
follows the Government’s approved data standard.
4.    
This recommendation seeks to ensure that the process
of keeping the Local Plan timetable up to date is as efficient as
possible in the context of new statutory requirements for doing
so3. Under Government’s new plan-making system, timetables
are more detailed (with a greater number of statutory steps to be
reported) and specific (e.g. indicating dates rather than
months/seasons for each step) than was previously the case.
Further, local planning authorities (LPAs) are required to ensure
their local plan timetable is reviewed and where necessary updated
on a more frequent basis (i.e. each month following the date on
which it is first published) rather than only at major milestones
as was previously the case. In this context, it is considered that
delegating the function of further revision and publication of the
Local Plan timetable as proposed will more easily enable compliance
with statutory requirements and support efficient decision-making
processes.
 
Other options considered and
rejected by the Executive:
 
Option 2: Not agreeing the
recommendations would lead to delay in progressing the Guildford
Local Plan. It may also risk the Council not meeting Government
requirements for commencing plan-making as set out in this report.
The Local Plan implementation funding, which is contingent on
meeting the earlier dates for the notice, and passing Gateway 1,
would also be at risk should this option be favoured.
 
Option 3: Agreeing
recommendations at 2.1.1, 2.1.2 and 2.1.3, but not 2.1.4 (regarding
delegating authority for future revision and publication of the
timetable) is an option open to the Executive. However, as more
frequent revision is now anticipated given the increased level of
detail within the Local Plan timetable (and required by the
regulations), delegation of this function is favoured. This would
enable efficient decision-making with sufficient
oversight.
 
Details of any conflict of
interest declared by the Leader or lead councillors and any
dispensation granted:
None.
topline: The Executive has decided to agree on the timetable for preparing the Guildford Local Plan under the Government's new plan-making system.

purpose:
To write off £214,000 as unrecoverable bad
debt.
content:
To write off £214,000 as unrecoverable bad
debt.

Decision:
1.      
Write off the outstanding debt of £214,332.50
owed to the Council;
2.      
uphold the Council’s right to pursue a claim
at a later date should a UK address for the landowner be
identified; and
3.      
note that the decision to write off the debt is only
an internal accounting adjustment and this decision does not
preclude the Council from recovering the debt at a later
date.
 
Reason(s):
 
1.    
The action taken under the planning and
environmental protection acts was approved by the Council in 2021.
The reports identified the owner of the land was absent and that
recovery of debt was unlikely.
2.    
In 2021 the Council used powers to act in default
under Section 79, Environmental Protection Act 1990 and Section 178
Town and Country Planning Act 1990, to clear the land of all
temporary living accommodation and structures, vehicles, animals
and equipment.
3.    
The action although costly was not only successful
in abating nuisance from smoke, it also resulted in the clearance
of all of the unauthorised uses on land with the exception of waste
deposits.
4.    
The responsibility for the enforcement of the waste
management regime is within the remits of both Surrey County
Council and the Environment Agency. The Council did not clear any
deposited waste from the site.
5.    
Despite the use of a debt recovery agency the
recovery of the outstanding debt of £214,332.50, covering the
bailiff and removal fees, has not shown any progress over the last
3 years.
6.    
The Council used a debt recovery company who
reported that they had no success in locating the owner. Whilst
communication was received from the owner’s son, he had no
formal interest in the land and denied any responsibility for the
costs.
7.    
The seizure of the land in light of the debt was not
considered prudent due to the restricted planning profile and the
potential contamination from waste deposited on this land and the
neighbouring area to the west.
 
 
Other options considered and
rejected by the Executive:
 
Option 1 - Request a Charge to
be placed on land at the Land Registry, for the value of
outstanding debt, providing a legitimate avenue to recover the debt

risk. This option is not recommended.

refinement if required.

purpose:

added to the capital programme
content:
Decision:
1.      
That full Council at its meeting on 12 May 2026 be
recommended to resolve to approve a budget of £3,297,300 to
be added to the capital programme, of which £1,387,000 is
LAHF Round 4 capital grant funding, with the balance being funded
from the Housing Revenue Account; and
 
2.      
Subject to Full Council approving the necessary
budget:
 
(a)             
To accept £1,387,000 of LAHF Round 4 grant
funding and agree to the forward financing of the acquisition of
six properties under this scheme; and
(b)            
To approve the scheme delivery profile as set out in
Exempt Appendix 1 to the report.
 
Reasons:
1.      
The project will facilitate the acquisition of homes
that will be used for temporary accommodation for homeless families
or for families on the Afghan Resettlement Programme. This aligns
with the Council’s objective of using the means available to
it to deliver decent and affordable homes for our residents as set
out in its Corporate Strategy 2024-2034.
2.      
The Council has been allocated a total of
£1,396,048 LAHF Round 4 funding.
3.      
Whilst the Council will be required to commit its
own funds to deliver the project, the initial financial appraisal
demonstrates that the Council-funded element of the budget is
recoverable via the rental income streams within an acceptable
period and is positive in terms of the cost to the HRA Business
Plan over 30 years.
 
Other options considered and
rejected by the Executive:
OPTION 1:
Do not accept LAHF Round 4 funding
allocation
The Council could choose to
decline the funding allocation but would lose the opportunity to
leverage this funding to subsidise the acquisition of six
additional homes during the funding period.
 
Details of any conflict of
interest declared by the Leader or lead councillors and any
dispensation granted:
None.
topline: The Executive Council has decided to approve a budget of £3,297,300 to acquire homes for temporary accommodation for homeless families and families on the Afghan Resettlement Programme.

purpose:
Replacement Boardwalk Riverside Nature
Reserve.
content:
Decision:
To approve the award of a
contract for Riverside Boardwalk Replacement works at Riverside
Nature Reserve, Guildford
to Keystone Environmental Ltd
for a period of five months, for an anticipated contract value of
£628,045 plus, optional extras up to a value of an additional
£12,250.
 
Reasons:

1.    
The recommended contractor achieved the highest
overall score in the tender evaluation, demonstrating superior
technical quality and methodology.

2.    
The submission provided strong environmental and
ecological management aligned with the sensitive nature of the
site.

3.    
The replacement of the existing boardwalk is
necessary as the current structure has deteriorated beyond repair
and presents an increasing risk to public safety if left
unaddressed.

4.    
Failure to proceed with the project would likely
result in restricted or unsafe access to the site, negatively
impacting residents’ ability to use and enjoy the nature
reserve.

5.    
There is a risk of reputational damage to the
Council if known safety issues are not addressed in a timely
manner, particularly in a well-used public and environmentally
designated site.

6.    
It is further recommended that approval is
progressed at the earliest opportunity, as the project needs to
commence in the spring period to ensure successful delivery. Any
delay in awarding the contract will impact the programme and is
likely to shift construction into October and November, which
represents the wettest part of the year.

7.    
The fen habitat is highly seasonal and becomes
significantly
waterlogged
during autumn and winter months, making it unsuitable for
construction activity. Delaying the start would therefore increase
the risk that the works cannot be undertaken safely or effectively
within the required timeframe.
 
Other options considered and
rejected by the Executive:
None
 
Details of any conflict of
interest declared by the Leader or lead councillors and any
dispensation granted:
None

The Leader made the following
announcements:
 
LGR update:
Surrey has reached an important
milestone in preparations for the new West and East Surrey
councils, as Parliament has approved the Surrey Structural Changes
Order.
This Order provides the legal
framework for the transition to two new unitary authorities,
responsible for all local services from 1 April 2027.
The priority throughout the
transition is to ensure residents, businesses and communities
continue to receive the support they need without
interruption.
Up-to-date information on Local
Government Reorganisation, including the forthcoming West and East
Surrey council elections, can be found on the Future Surrey
website and our social media channels.
 
North Street
regeneration:
The next North Street
regeneration Community Liaison Group Meeting will take place on
Wednesday 15 April, 6pm to 7.15pm at St Saviours Church on
Woodbridge Road.
The session will
feature:
·       
an update on the development
·       
news on community activities and
·       
a special spotlight on careers in
construction.
Councillors will receive an
invitation from St Edward - if you would like to attend the event,
please email info@housegroup.co.uk
 
Westborough and Park Barn
Better Homes Programme:
We’ve launched a major
new initiative to transform homes and community spaces in
Westborough and Park Barn, and we’re inviting residents to
help shape the future of their neighbourhood.
We’re starting community
engagement for the Westborough and Park Barn Better Homes Programme
- an important step in our commitment to providing high quality
Council homes and a thriving community for our
residents.
Over the coming months,
we’ll invite residents to share their ideas, priorities and
concerns. We’re also establishing a new resident engagement
group to help guide this important programme of work.
Further information has been
sent to households in the project area and is available on
our website.

purpose:
This review of the Housing Allocations Policy
aims to ensure that the policy remains fair, transparent, and
aligned with current legal frameworks, local priorities, and
housing needs. The review considers recent legislative changes,
shifts in housing demand, and feedback from service users and
stakeholders. The goal is to deliver a revised policy that supports
efficient housing management, reflects local priorities, and
promotes fairness and social inclusion.
content:
Decision:
To approve the revised Housing
Allocations Scheme, as set out in Appendix 1.
 
Reason(s):
1.                
Guildford Borough Council’s Housing
Allocations Scheme last had a full review in August 2014. The
scheme has been updated to remain complaint with legislation and
guidance, with reviews in March 2019, August 2024 and May 2025,
however a full review is due.
2.                
Following the adoption of a new Housing Strategy and
a Homelessness Prevention and Rough Sleeping Strategy in April
2025, a review of the Housing Allocations Scheme is a natural
progression of reviewing and updating service
arrangements.
3.                
This review will include any learning from recent
case studies, align our approach to our partners at Waverley in
steps towards Local Government Restructure, and encompass the
provisions we have committed to as part of the Surrey House Project
for care leavers.
4.                
The update of the scheme forms part of and supports
the work on the Housing Improvement Programme, as well as
contributing to the ambitions and priorities set out in the
Corporate Plan.
 
Other options considered and
rejected by the Executive:
1.           
To require further consultation and/or review on the
Housing Allocations Scheme and bring the scheme back for subsequent
review. This option is not recommended as it would delay the
implementation of improvements and progression with wider
improvements to the service.
2.           
To carry out a review that looks to implement more
major changes. This option is not recommended. With Local
Government Reorganisation expected, it is recommended that to carry
out a full, major review of the Housing Allocation Scheme would be
a significant use of resources given the likelihood of further
changes when reorganisation takes place.
3.           
Do nothing and keep the existing Allocation Scheme
the same. This option is not recommended. A failure to implement
the changes identified following the review would risk the Council
failing to comply with legislation, case law and Government
guidance, and would miss an opportunity for the Council to achieve
the objectives of its Corporate Plan and Housing
Strategy.
 
Details of any conflict of
interest declared by the Leader or lead councillors and any
dispensation granted:
None.
topline: The Executive has decided to approve the revised Housing Allocations Scheme.

purpose:
To consider and to adopt the
strategy.
content:
Decision:

1.      To note and agree the
business case set out in this report; and

2.      To adopt the 2026-2031 GBC
Housing Asset Management Strategy.
 
Reason(s):
1.           
To ensure the housing stock remains safe, compliant
and fit for purpose. The Strategy sets out a fully funded programme
to achieve and maintain 100% Decent Homes compliance by December
2026, alongside strengthened building safety, statutory compliance
and robust stock condition data. This will protect residents,
reduce risk exposure and ensure regulatory obligations are
consistently met.
2.           
To note investment that secures long?term asset
sustainability and financial viability. The 30?year £331.47m
investment plan and the five?year £61.96m programme are
aligned with HRA financial capacity, enabling strategic
procurement, planned and cost?effective management of
residents’ homes, minimising responsive repair demand, and
ensuring value for money
3.           
To support delivery of the Council’s strategic
objectives and resident priorities. The Strategy directly aligns
with the Corporate Strategy and Housing Strategy and reflects
resident consultation results, particularly around energy
efficiency, safety, modern facilities and neighbourhood
improvements.
4.           
To provide a robust framework for future
decision?making, regeneration and asset rationalisation. The
Strategy introduces structured sustainability modelling and Net
Present Value (NPV) analysis to guide investment, redevelopment and
disposal decisions. This will be critical in managing ageing stock,
identifying regeneration opportunities, and preparing for Local
Government Reorganisation.
 
Other options considered and
rejected by the Executive:
Option 1 – To not approve
the HAMS 2026-2031. This would mean the Council would be in breach
of the expectations of the Regulator for Social Housing and not
have visibility of investment requirements over the long
term.
 
Details of any conflict of
interest declared by the Leader or lead councillors and any
dispensation granted:
None.

2024-25 Annual Report (as set in Appendix 1 to the report) to allow
it to be published, as statutorily required.
 
2.        To formally
advertise amendments to the Guildford Off-street Parking Places
Order 2008 (as amended) to include the following:
 
(a) the
introduction of parking controls at Gardner Road Garages, Guildford
to prevent parking within the garage area other than within the
garages themselves; and
(b) the
revocation of the order at Onslow Park and Ride car park
 
and
if no representations are received, for the amendments to be made.
If representations are received, in line with the Council’s
Constitution, for these to be considered by the Joint Assistant
Director of Commercial Services, in consultation with the Lead
Councillor for Economy and Place, and a decision made to either
make, revise or not progress the proposed amendments.
 
Reasons:
1.           
Local authority parking enforcement authorities must
publish an annual report of their parking operations, revenue and
enforcement, in order to comply with the requirements of the
Traffic Management Act 2004 and the accompanying statutory
guidance, Appendix 1 provides this for the FY2024-25.
2.           
A concern has been raised about inconsiderate
parking in the garage area at Gardner Road. Although this does not
presently cause access issues for garage users, it is considered
appropriate to introduce a traffic regulation order to resolve the
present issue and prevent it from developing further.
3.           
The introduction of a TRO, which will not include
any marked parking bays, will effectively prevent vehicles being
parked anywhere within the communal areas of the garage block.
Although, strictly speaking unnecessary, this could be further
supplemented by the introduction of double yellow lines to
highlight the fact that parking is prevented. This will reduce the
risk of inconsiderate parking blocking garages and access. However,
it should be noted that the formalisation of parking will
invariably reduce garage users’ flexibility, in so far that
they would no longer be able to park their vehicles elsewhere in
the garage area, other than within their garages. However, this
arrangement would be similar to the arrangements that are already
in place at Bedford Sheds, Falcon Road and Stoke Fields garage
areas.
4.           
As the Onslow Park and Ride car park site has
reverted back to the landowner, the University of Surrey (UoS), it
is considered appropriate to revoke the TRO covering this car park.
TROs can only apply in locations where the enforcement authority
(GBC) has an ‘interest’. As the site is no longer
leased from the UoS by GBC, it no longer has an
‘interest’ in the land.

 
Other options considered and
rejected by the Executive:
The Executive could choose not
to advertise the proposed amendments to the TRO, but if it were not
to do so, it would not resolve the issues raised. Therefore, it is
recommended that these amendments are made.
 
Details of any conflict of
interest declared by the Leader or lead councillors and any
dispensation granted:
None.

compliance with relevant Procurement Legislation and the

used

environmental and climate change impact, social value and
modern-day slavery risk.

including how contract management will ensure that the Council

therefore being more agile in the approval process in relation to
procurement activity.

approval for any consequent contract award which would be a Key
Decision will be sought by a separate report, unless authority is
specifically delegated to an officer

Ash
residents can give their views on proposed Neighbourhood
Plan
Residents in Ash can help shape
the future of their community by taking part in a consultation on a
proposed Neighbourhood Plan.  This is a
real opportunity for the Ash community to directly influence the
places where they live and work. The more people who get involved,
the stronger the final Plan will be.
 
The consultation will run until
12noon on Monday 9 March.
More
information on the Plan and an online response form are available
on our consultation website.
 
Community Governance Review for Guildford
Town
The community governance review for Guildford Town launched
on Tuesday 6 February 2026. Households in the ten wards being
consulted have received booklets telling them about it. There is a
social media campaign to encourage feedback from
residents.
 
On Wednesday 4 February, we will be hosting an online
presentation at 7.30pm for residents who might have questions. You
can register for this event on our website.  We are also holding a series of pop-up events
including:
·     
outside the Guildhall 10am to 2pm on Tuesday 3
February 2026
·     
at The Hive from 10am to 1pm on Thursday 26 February
2026
 
Experience Guildford has also
kindly offered to take some of our CGR booklets to the re-fresher
fair at the University of Surrey on Friday 6 February
2026
More information is on our
website. Searching for ‘Community Governance Review stage
2’.
 
Electric Theatre roundtable event
The Leader thanked all the
performers, venue operators, arts groups and other stakeholders,
who participated in the roundtable event that we hosted earlier
this month. Led by an independent facilitator, the session was
designed to bring the community together to work together to shape
ideas and develop shared values for the theatre's
future.
Participants demonstrated real
energy and passion throughout the day and provided valuable
insights. A report on this would be considered by the Executive
later this year.

To find out more about the roundtable visit the newsroom of our
website.
 
New Guildford Climate Hub launches
The Council had recently launched a new online resource to
help residents, businesses and community groups better understand
climate change and how they can take action. The ‘Guildford
Climate Hub’ brings together clear, trusted information in
one place. It explains:
·     
what climate change
means for Guildford,
·     
what we are doing to
address it
·     
and how everyone in
the borough can play their part.
 
It also highlights local support, events and community
groups who are making a difference. This new website supports one
of our key priorities; to make Guildford a more sustainable
borough.
 
Business Question Time
The fourth Guildford and Waverley Business Question Time
will take place on Monday 16 March at the Harbour Hotel. It will be
a free event bringing local businesses together to network, share
ideas and hear from leading voices.
 
This year’s theme would be Resilience in the Digital
Age, with a keynote from Jane Frankland MBE, a renowned
cyber?security expert. Businesses will also have the chance to quiz
a diverse panel covering digital transformation, sustainability,
innovation and women in business.
topline: The council has decided to allow residents in Ash to have a say in shaping their community through a consultation on a proposed Neighbourhood Plan.

bands.

(b)    To agree the

explains the conditions and uncertainties that will impact service
delivery in future years

content:
Decision:
1.   To approve the draft
Tenancy Strategy as set out in Appendix 2 to the report submitted
to the Executive.
 
2.   To delegate authority to
the Joint Assistant Director for Housing to make minor amendments
to the Tenancy Strategy in line with future regulatory or
legislative changes in consultation with the relevant portfolio
holder.
 
Reasons:
1.   The Localism Act 2011
requires every local housing authority to prepare and publish a
tenancy strategy and to keep it under review.
2.   Guildford Borough
Council’s Tenancy Strategy was last updated in          
2020 and is therefore due for review. Guildford’s housing
services are currently undergoing significant transformation
through the Housing Improvement Programme. In addition, the Council
adopted the Housing Strategy and the Homelessness Prevention and
Rough Sleeping Strategy in April 2025. To ensure alignment with
these strategic priorities and reflect best practice, it is
recommended that the Tenancy Strategy is now reviewed and
updated.
3.   Updating the Tenancy
Strategy is part of the Housing Service’s commitment to
improvement and delivering the corporate priority of ‘Decent
and Affordable Homes’. Work is now underway to review and
update the Council’s Tenancy Policy to reflect our approach
to granting, managing and terminating tenancies.
 
Other options considered and
rejected by the Executive:
2.      
Do Not Approve the Draft Tenancy Strategy
This option was not recommended as it would leave the existing
Tenancy Strategy in place. However, the current document does not
fully reflect the Council’s updated strategic priorities, nor
recent legislative changes, and therefore carries a risk of
inconsistency, reduced effectiveness, and potential
non-compliance.
3.      
Defer Consideration of the Draft Tenancy
Strategy
This
option was not recommended as it would maintain the status quo in
the short term but could delay the alignment of tenancy policy with
the Council’s wider housing objectives. It may also reduce
the Council’s ability to provide a clear and consistent
framework for registered providers and residents, result in us
entering Local Government Reorganisation without and up to date
strategy in place and would not address the risks identified in the
report.
 
Details of any conflict of
interest declared by the Leader or lead councillors and any
dispensation granted:
None.

November 2025 and the contract for the West expired on 5 December
2025. At present, we are currently meeting demand for this service
on a reactive basis. It is not advisable to maintain this approach,
given the peak period for this service is approaching and there is
a need to put a formal compliant contract in place to ensure that
we meet our statutory duty.
2.    
If we do not enter into these contracts, the Council
will fail in providing its statutory Gas and Boiler Servicing
requirements.
3.    
The Council is preparing a tender for a longer-term
contract for each area, which is envisaged to be awarded within the
12 months period. It is imperative that whilst the council is
procuring a new long-term contract, that we continue to service all
domestic boilers in our properties.
4.    
A waiver has been put in place for each of the
expired contracts to cover the period following expiry until
commencement of the interim solutions.
5.    
Additionally, the costs for demobilisation of
current contractors and cost of system integration and mobilisation
of new contract for a short period would outweigh any benefit from
bringing in any potential new supplier.
6.    
Value for money is demonstrated by continuity of the
service via the incumbent suppliers under a compliant call off
contract against Fusion 21 Framework Heating, Renewables, and
Electrical Framework Lot 1.
 
Other options considered and
rejected by the Executive:
1.    
Do nothing – This option was dismissed because
continuing with the expired contracts presents a breach against the
Council’s Contract Procedure Rules. Furthermore, if the
supplier walked away from the contract, this would prevent the
Council from meeting its statutory duties under GSIUR, HHSRS, and
the Decent Homes Standard. It would place tenants at risk due to
unsafe or unmaintained gas installations, increase asset risk
across the housing stock, and expose the Council to potential
financial and reputational harm.
2.    
Extend Previous Contracts – This option was
dismissed because the existing contracts have now expired and
cannot legally be extended. Under the Public Contracts Regulations
2015 (PCR 2015), extending an expired contract would constitute a
direct award without competition, which is a breach of procurement
law. Proceeding in this way would expose the Council to significant
legal, financial, and reputational risks, including potential
challenge from the market. As such, this option is neither lawful
nor appropriate.
 
Details of any conflict of
interest declared by the Leader or lead councillors and any
dispensation granted:
None.
topline: The Executive has decided to award contracts for domestic gas boiler servicing to ensure compliance with statutory duties and maintain safe gas installations.

content:
The Leader made the following
announcements:
 
Following the first stage of
consultation on the Community Governance Review for the unparished
urban area of Guildford, the Council had agreed to proceed to the
second stage of consultation, which was launched on Tuesday 6
January.
 
There are currently ten wards
in central Guildford that are not represented by a parish or town
council. We’re proposing the creation of a new parish
council, so that residents across central Guildford have elected
parish councillors making decisions about local, parish-level
services.
 
The consultation is available
online and households in the currently unparished area will receive
a booklet next week through the post. This will outline the draft
proposals and ask residents to share their views. We’re
hosting an online event on Wednesday 4 February at 7.30pm and also
planning a couple of pop-up events where residents can find out
more.
More information is on our
website. Searching for ‘Community Governance Review stage
2’.
 
We’re installing new,
user-friendly parking technology in our town centre car parks this
month. The work began yesterday at the Tunsgate Car Park, which is
the first to have new payment machines installed. The machines will
make it quicker and easier for drivers to pay for their parking.
There’ll be card, contactless, cash and app payments
available and no need for visitors to use paper tickets. The new
technology will be installed in 18 car parks around Guildford and
the work will take a few weeks to complete.
 
One of our council’s key
priorities is to make Guildford a more prosperous borough. Projects
like this, which make parking easier for residents and visitors,
support our economy and encourage more people to come into our
beautiful town.
topline: The Council has decided to proceed with the creation of a new parish council for the unparished urban area of Guildford.

content:
To stop issuing flexible tenancies to new and current
council tenants whilst a review of the tenancy policy is
undertaken

Approve an amendment to the
Council’s ‘Tenancy Strategy 2020’ and Tenancy
Policy to enable the temporary suspension of the Council’s
policy of awarding flexible (fixed-term) tenancies for new general
needs lettings for a six month period.


1.    
To enable an amendment to the Council’s
existing policy, so as to provide a consistent and secure tenancy
offer to new tenants while the Council reviews its ‘Tenancy
Strategy 2020’ and Tenancy Policy.
 

2.    
To reduce administrative complexity and improve
tenant satisfaction.
 

3.    
To align with the direction of national regulation
and expectations around tenant stability and
empowerment.
 

Option 1 - Continue issuing flexible tenancies (do
nothing)
·        
This risks tenant insecurity and contradicts the
Council’s emerging strategic direction.
·        
Administering flexible tenancies requires additional
resource and monitoring.
Option 2 - Suspend flexible tenancies (recommended)
·        
Provides clarity and consistency during the Tenancy
Strategy and Tenancy Policy review.
·        
Aligns with current expectations around tenant
security and simplifies operations.
Option 3 - End flexible tenancies immediately and change policy
without a full review
·        
Not recommended due to governance and consultation
requirements.
 

None.

Council Constitution Part
3
Leader/Executive (paragraph
6)
To make decisions on all
executive matters within the approved budget and policy framework
and on all other matters which are not the responsibility of any
other part of the Council by virtue of the law or this
Constitution.

content:
Decision:
1.           
To resolve:
 
1.1           
To note the Secretary of State’s decision to
proceed with two unitary councils for Surrey, as set out in the
letter at Appendix 1 to this report;
 
1.2           
To approve, subject to the similar approval by
Surrey County Council, Waverley Borough Council, Runnymede Borough
Council, Spelthorne Borough Council, Surrey Heath Borough Council
and Woking Borough Council, the establishment of a West Surrey
Joint Committee, in accordance with section 101(5) of the Local
Government Act 1972 and pursuant to the requirements of the draft
Surrey (Structural Changes) Order 2026, to be entered into between
Guildford Borough Council and the other principal authorities
referenced in this paragraph;
 
1.3           
To nominate the Leader of Guildford Borough Council
as the Guildford Borough Council representative on the West Surrey
Joint Committee and to recommend their appointment to
Council;
 
1.4           
To recommend to Council that it delegates the
nomination and appointment of any substitute member on the West
Surrey Joint Committee to the Leader of the Council; 
 
1.5           
To approve the draft terms of reference of the West
Surrey Joint Committee as set out in Appendix 2 to this report, and
to delegate to the Monitoring Officer, in consultation with the
Leader of the Council, the authority to make minor
amendments;
 
1.6           
To note that whilst the West Surrey Joint Committee
is established by resolution of all current councils in the
geography of the proposed West Surrey Council, on a voluntary
basis, upon the enactment of the Surrey (Structural Changes) Order
2026 the West Surrey Joint Committee shall become the  joint committee required to be established under
the provisions of that legislation and that this will be
constituted and established under the provisions of section 101 (5)
of the Local Government Act 1972 and pursuant to the requirements
of the Surrey (Structural Changes) Order 2026.
 
1.7           
To approve the delegation of all Guildford Borough
Council Executive functions, within the terms of reference of the
West Surrey Joint Committee, to the West Surrey Joint
Committee.
 
2.           
To recommend that the Council resolves:
 

2.1        To take into
account the recommendations of the Joint Standards
Committee;

2.2        To note,
subject to the decision of the Executive, the resolution to
establish a West Surrey Joint Committee, subject to the decision of
other councils, between the principal authorities of Surrey County
Council, Guildford Borough Council, Waverley Borough Council,
Spelthorne Borough Council, Runnymede Borough Council, Surrey Heath
Borough Council, and Woking Borough Council.

2.3        To note the
Executive’s approval of the draft terms of reference for the
West Surrey Joint Committee, as set out in Appendix 2;

2.4        To note the
Executive’s recommendation of the Leader as the nominated
Guildford Borough Council to represent Guildford Borough Council on
the West Surrey Joint Committee and resolve to make such
appointment;

2.5        To delegate
authority to the Leader of the Council to nominate and appoint any
substitute member to represent Guildford Borough Council on the
West Surrey Joint Committee;

2.6        To delegate
all non-Executive functions relating to Guildford Borough Council,
within the remit of the West Surrey Joint Committee, to the West
Surrey Joint Committee;

2.7        To delegate to
the Monitoring Officer the authority to make any necessary and
consequential amendments, arising from the resolutions of the
Executive and the Council in this matter, to the Guildford Borough
Council constitution.
 
Reason(s):

1.           
As Surrey transitions to two new unitary local
authorities, Guildford Borough Council remains committed to
maintaining openness and transparency with residents and wider
partners, which includes regular updates to members on local
government reorganisation.

2.           
The recommendations in this report are made to
support the desire to be well prepared for local government
reorganisation and to be able to support the West Surrey Council
shadow authority from May 2026.
 
Other options considered and
rejected by the Executive:

1.           
To wait until the Council is mandated to establish a
West Surrey Joint Committee by the SCO in March 2026.

2.           
To appoint a West Surrey Joint Committee but on
different terms of reference from those expected in the draft
SCO.
 
Details of any conflict of
interest declared by the Leader or lead councillors and any
dispensation granted:
None.

content:
Decision:

1.                    
Note the comments of the Overview and Scrutiny
Committee meeting held on 18 November 2025 and set out at paragraph
11 of this report; and
 

2.                    
Delegate Authority to the Joint Assistant Director
for Assets and Property, in consultation with the Portfolio Holder
for Finance and the Joint Strategic Director for Finance and
Resources, to commence formal marketing and to negotiate terms for
a disposal of Land at Salt Box Road, Worplesdon at best
consideration and to enter into all relevant legal documentation
required to complete the sale.
 
Reason(s):
To enable the Council to
generate capital receipts through the sale of approved property and
land assets to contribute to the £50m (net) target, as set
out in the Financial Recovery Plan to reduce Council debt and to
achieve a sustainable financial position.
 
Other options considered and
rejected by the Executive:

1.                    
Do nothing and adopt a business as usual approach to this asset
continuing to seek to licence the land for grazing use and
generating (limited) rental income. This option would not provide a
capital receipt to contribute towards the targeted capital receipts
of £50m and may also result in the Council incurring future
revenue or capital expenditure to manage the land in the
future. 
 

2.                    
Continue to explore the option for development of a
Solar Farm on the land which may assist in potentially offsetting
the Council’s requirement to purchase carbon credits to the
value of £154,000 over a 20 year project life span. This option would
however fail to deliver a capital receipt to contribute towards the
£50M target agreed as part of the Financial Recovery Plan.
Further, the feasibility study undertaken suggested any positive
return was marginal at best when other external factors were
considered.
 
Details of any conflict of
interest declared by the Leader or lead councillors and any
dispensation granted:
None.

purpose:
To approve a budget from the Housing Revenue
Account (HRA) Capital Fund for a 5-year kitchen and bathroom
improvement contract which will be procured jointly and in
collaboration with Waverley Borough Council.
content:
Decision:

1.                    
Note and agree the business case set out in this
report;

2.                    
Subject to Council approving the budget to delegate
authority to the Joint Strategic Director of Finance &
Resources, in consultation with the Joint Assistant Director of
Housing and the Lead Councillor for Finance, to commence a joint
procurement with Waverley Borough Council and to subsequently award
a contract for 3 Years with the option to extend for a further 1+1
year, kitchen and bathroom contract in compliance with the Contract
Procedure Rules and within the approved budgets; and

3.                    
Recommend to full Council, meeting 9 December 2025,
to approve Housing Revenue Account (HRA) Capital Funding of
£12.5m for replacement kitchens and bathrooms between 2026/27
and 2031/32
 
Reason(s):

1.                    
Social Housing Landlords have an ongoing requirement
to meet and maintain the Governments’ Decent Homes Standard.
Replacing and improving components, such as kitchens and bathrooms,
that are old and in poor condition, help us meet that
requirement. 

2.                    
GBC’s current decent homes data indicates that
c260 kitchens and c130 bathrooms will become non-decent annually
over the 5-year horizon. 

3.                    
Procuring and having in place a long-term kitchen
and bathroom contract will allow GBC to efficiently and
economically delivery kitchen and bathroom improvements to
resident’s homes. 

4.                    
The Procurement Strategy for GBC and WBC is to
wherever possible procure services and works jointly to utilise
economies of scale, procure services efficiently and economically,
and deliver effective and consistent services to
residents.

5.                    
Waverley Borough Council agreed to commence the
procurement for a Kitchen and Bathrooms contract on the 1 April
2025, for a budget of £12.6m, which is sufficient to cover a
five-year contract.
 
Other options considered and
rejected by the Executive:
Option 1 - Defer procurement of
a longer-term contract and extend the term of the interim
arrangement, subject to satisfactory performance and compliance
with procurement regulations
 
Details of any conflict of
interest declared by the Leader or lead councillors and any
dispensation granted:
None.

content:
1.Approve the award of the contract for the construction of
the Internal Estate Road Phase 2 to Winvic Construction
Ltd.
 
2. To delegate to the Strategic Director of Economy,
Planning and Place, in consultation with the Lead Councillor for
Regeneration and Lead Councillor for Finance, authority to enter
into such other contracts and legal agreements connected with the
Internal Estate Road Phase 2 project as may be necessary in
compliance with Procurement Procedure Rules, the Council’s
Constitution and within the approved budget.

Decision:
Waive the Council’s
Contract Procudure Rules and, in doing so, approve the direct award
of the contract for the construction of the Internal Estate Road
Phase 2 to Winvic Construction Ltd.
 
Reason(s):

1.                    
A tender exercise was undertaken and Winvic were the
successful bidder. There were delays to the programme as a result
of obtaining necessary consents, programming and further technical
design work which were beyond the control of the Council or Winvic.
As a result it was not possible to enter the contract as tendered
with Winvic and the procurement has been abandoned.

2.                    
It is now proposed that the Council directly awards
a contract for these works to Winvic as all outstanding matters
have been resolved.  Procurement and
legal advice is that this is not a covered procurement given the
value but it must still comply with our Contract Procedure Rules
which would usually require competition.

3.                    
The recommendation in this report is therefore that
Executive waive the Contract Procedure Rules to directly award the
contract to Winvic to support the broader Weyside Urban Village
programme by facilitating the delivery of essential highways
infrastructure, critical to enabling access across the entire site.
There is a limited window of opportunity to carry out these works
in Q4 2025/26, between the completion of the construction elements
at the new Sewage Treatment Works and the operational commencement
of the new GBC depot.
 
Other options considered and
rejected by the Executive:
Do nothing.
 
Details of any conflict of
interest declared by the Leader or lead councillors and any
dispensation granted:
None.

content:
Decision:
Approve the award of a contract
for EICR Inspections and Remedial Works to Pilon Limited for an
initial three (3) year term, with the option for Guildford Borough
Council to extend for an initial period of one (1) year and then a
further option to extend for another one (1) year (total maximum
five (5) years), for an anticipated contract value of
£4,137,473.74 (four million, one hundred thirty-seven
thousand, four hundred seventy-three pounds and seventy-four pence)
plus inflation, subject to annual review. 
 
Reason(s):

1.                    
The 18th Edition Wiring Regulations - IET BS7671
require landlords to undertake regular electrical condition reports
and recommend that they are undertaken at least every 5-years, or
upon new tenancies, within homes, and communal areas.

2.                    
The EICR Inspections and Remedial
Works contract is required to enable Guildford Borough
Council (GBC) to carry out this regulatory requirement.

3.                    
Under this contract 4,981 properties have been
considered, which require; periodic inspections on a 5-year cycle
or at change of occupancy; smoke and heat detection at least once
every 5 years; and rewiring works on approximately 17% of the
properties, as this is required on a 25 to 30 year life span. These
numbers will fluctuate based on changes in stock and management
responsibility, e.g. sales, acquisitions, and
demolition.

4.                    
GBC needs to maintain the current programme of EICRs
through an external contractor under a new contract to ensure we
maintain compliance with the regulations and to minimise the risk
to residents, staff, and properties.

5.                    
Valid electrical inspection condition reports enable
us to demonstrate compliance with regulatory requirements, by
identifying and/or preventing significant electrical hazards. It
also supports the requirements of the Building Safety Act 2022 and
The Fire Safety Act 2021, ensuring they do not contribute to the
risk and spread of fire in multi-storey, multi-occupancy rented
accommodation.
 
Other options considered and
rejected by the Executive:
Do nothing.
Details of any conflict of
interest declared by the Leader or lead councillors and any
dispensation granted:
None.

purpose:
Request Waverley Borough Council to discharge
those Finance functions of Guildford Borough Council which are
Executive functions, with effect from 1 April 2026.
content:
Decision:
 

1.                    
Agree that Waverley Borough Council discharge on
behalf of Guildford Borough Council such of its Finance functions
which are Executive functions, with effect from 1 April
2026.

2.                    
Agree to the creation of new joint posts to deliver
Finance Services to both Waverley Borough Council and Guildford
Borough Council and delegate authority to the Joint Assistant
Director for Finance to implement a joint staffing structure within
the approved budget.

3.                    
That the Joint
Executive Committee recommends that Guildford Borough Council
resolves to:

4.                    
Request that Waverley Borough Council discharge on
behalf of Guildford Borough Council such of its Finance functions
which are Council functions as set out in paragraph 12.2.3 with
effect from 1 April 2026.

5.                    
That the Joint
Executive Committee recommends that Waverley Borough Council
resolves to:

6.                    
Accept the request from Guildford Borough Council
that Waverley Borough Council discharge on behalf of Guildford
Borough Council such of its Finance functions which are Council
functions as set out in paragraph 12.2.3 with effect from 1 April
2026.

7.                    
That the Joint
Executive Committee recommends to Waverley and Guildford Borough
Councils that they:

8.                    
Note that the joint staffing structure for delivery
of Finance functions will consist of staff transferred from
Guildford Borough Council on 1 April 2026 and Waverley Borough
Council staff.

9.                    
Authorise the Strategic Director of Democracy, Law
and People in consultation with the co-Chairs of the Joint
Governance Committee to update the Inter-Authority Agreement to
include provisions that ensure all decisions in relation to the
arrangements are made by both Guildford Borough Council and
Waverley Borough Council.
 
Reason(s):
 

1.                    
To enable Finance functions to operate in an
efficient and cost-effective way, making use of the resources
available and sharing experience and knowledge with the opportunity
to provide more specialist skills across both authorities, leading
to increased efficiency, improved performance and service delivery
with an expansion of knowledge for individuals and sharing of best
practice.

2.                    
To provide increased resilience, capacity and
capability in the provision of statutory financial services as
there will be a more flexible pool of officers delivering the
services across both Waverley Borough Council and Guildford Borough
Council. The current structure has many single points of failure
when staff go on agreed leave of absence. An outcome of this puts
serious strain on the resources that remain to cover and increases
the risk of service delivery failure. 
This new structure will provide additional resilience to cover
sickness absence, annual leave, vacancies or increased workload
should this be required.

3.                    
The shared Finance service is within the approved
budget.  Increased capacity and
collaborative working through standardised processes and procedures
should see improvements in the collection of income and in the
service response to our external customers, ensuring backlogs in
the provision of Housing Benefits and Revenues and Benefits
services are minimised.   

4.                    
To ensure that joint working is undertaken in a
consistent manner and in accordance with existing HR policies for
such posts and the Inter-Authority Agreement between the two
authorities for the sharing of staff.

5.                    
To reduce dependency on external resources and
further implement succession planning and career development which
will provide opportunities for an increase in internal promotion
appointments for existing staff to vacant posts.
 
Other options considered and
rejected by the Joint Executive Committee:
 
Option 1 Do nothing
Option 3 Do Collaboration with
savings of £0.575m.
 
Details of any conflict of
interest declared by the Leaders or lead councillors and any
dispensation granted:
None.

content:
Decision:
To Approve the grant of a
five-year lease to Surrey County Council at a rent of
£142,040 per annum, subject to a mutual rolling break option
on six months prior written notice and no rent review.
 
Reason(s):
1.           
The
proposed terms represent best consideration.
2.           
The
proposed annual rent secures an income stream for the Council for 5
years and avoids vacant property costs.
3.           
The grant
of the proposed lease ensures continuity of occupation and
demonstrates effective management of the portfolio.
 
Other options considered and
rejected by the Executive:
To terminate the Tenancy at
Will that will be entered into at the expiry of the current lease
and not enter into the proposed lease, thereby leaving the property
empty for an indefinite period and costing the Council void
property costs including business rates, utility charges and
repairs and maintenance. As a partner organisation, this could
leave SCC in difficulty if no suitable alternative accommodation is
available. The tenant currently uses the office space to
accommodate teams from their Adult Social Care service.

interest declared by the Leader or lead councillors and any
dispensation granted:
None.

the property on the open market to find an alternative occupier.
This option comes with increased risk in terms of the time it will
take to find a suitable occupier, the costs of marketing the
property and the vacant property costs.

content:
The Leader made the following
announcements.
 
The latest on Local Government
Reorganisation in Surrey
Last week, the Government
decided to replace the current 12 Surrey councils with two new
unitary authorities.
The Government's announcement
on Local Government Reorganisation marks a significant moment for
Surrey. While we supported the proposal for three unitary councils
in the county, our priority remains clear - doing what is best for
our residents. We'll continue to work with councils across the
county and our partners to help create new authorities that deliver
for our communities into the future.
We'll keep our residents
updated as Local Government Reorganisation progresses, and the
latest information can also be found on the Surrey LGR
Hub.
 
North Street Construction
Update
We have been notified of a
24-hour road closure starting on Monday 10 November and lasting
until Friday 12 December. There will be no through route from
Friary Passage to North Street or Phoenix Court for general
traffic. This closure will facilitate work including the
reconstruction of the taxi rank next to McDonald’s, an
adjustment of the kerbline and repaving of the
footpaths.
During this time, access to
Friary Passage will be restricted to deliveries, servicing and
refuse. Access will be closed to food delivery drivers (including
Deliveroo/Uber Eats style mopeds and cyclists). You should all have
received a more detailed email from St Edward on this; however, the
full information and diversion route can also be viewed on the
dedicated website - northstreetregeneration.co.uk
 
Service of
Remembrance
The nation will commemorate
Remembrance Sunday this weekend and honour the sacrifices made by
our Armed Forces and their families. Our Borough Service of
Remembrance will take place at Holy Trinity Church at 9.45am. This
will be followed by a parade to the Castle Grounds, where we will
hold the two minute silence and lay wreaths at the war
memorials.
On Armistice Day (Tuesday 11
November) a short ceremony will take place outside the
Guildhall. Residents and visitors are welcome to gather from
10.50am on Guildford High Street and observe the two minute silence
at 11am. There are also many other Remembrance events you can join
across our borough.
 
Update on The Electric
Theatre
We are about to launch a
community survey to ask residents and groups for their views on the
future of The Electric Theatre. We’ll also be running three
pop-up sessions in Guildford to hear directly from local
people.
Our goal is to find a future
that:
·       
reflects the needs and ideas of our
community
·       
can be effectively maintained for years to
come
·       
continues to inspire creativity and the arts in
Guildford.
We want to make sure that any
decision the Council makes is informed by our community, so would
like to hear everyone’s views. Look out for more information
in our newsroom and on our social media channels very
soon.
 
Festive Fun Day
A reminder that we’ll
once again be stepping into Christmas in Guildford with our Festive
Family Fun Day. This free, family extravaganza will take place in
the town centre on Sunday 16 November from 11am to 4pm.
The event will transform
Guildford into a winter wonderland bursting with joy, music, and
magical moments. Full event listings and updates are available on
the VisitSurrey and
Experience
Guildford websites.

content:
Decision:

1. Approve
commencement of the procurement process for the projects listed in
Appendix 1 to this report.

2.
Delegate authority to the Joint Strategic Director for Finance and
Resources, having consulted with the Lead Councillor for Finance
and upon selection of a successful contractor, to award the
following contracts listed in Appendix 1:
a)    Advanced Electricity
Metering & Data Services Contract;
b)   Minor Works – Rodboro
walkway paving Contract; and
c)    Electric Taxi
Project.
Reason(s):

1.      
The
Executive is required to approve, prior to their commencement, all
procurement activity which may require a key decision for the
contract award. It is good governance to seek approval by providing
Executive with a summary of all proposed procurements that may
result in a key decision prior to procurement procedures formally
commencing.

2.      
Planning
procurement activity ensures:
•     effective
stakeholder management?
•     effective
procurement and sourcing?
•     compliance
with relevant Procurement Legislation and the Council’s own
Contract Procedure Rules??
•     there is
consideration on how contract price is to be managed in contract
and what contract price model will be used?
•     our
procurement is ethical by considering factors such as environmental
and climate change impact, social value and modern-day slavery
risk.??

•     how best value is to be achieved
is clearly defined including how contract management will ensure
that the Council attains best value during the life of the
contract.

3.      
This
report will avoid the need to submit multiple individual requests
for approval to procure and award contracts, therefore being more
agile in the approval process in relation to procurement
activity.

4.      
When a
procurement activity is concluded Executive approval for any
consequent contract award which would be a key decision will be
sought by a separate report, unless authority is specifically
delegated to an officer.
Other options considered and rejected by the
Executive:
Bringing each individual item to the Executive, which would
incur more time and cost writing individual reports.

lead councillors and any dispensation granted:
None.

content:
Decision:

1.      
Establish
a Joint Executive Committee with Waverley Borough Council’s
Executive, (subject to the decision of the Executive of Waverley
Borough Council), with the terms of reference as set out at
Appendix 1 to this report; and

2.      
That the
Executive recommends that the Standards Committee resolves to
‘Note the establishment of the new Joint Executive Committee
with Waverley Borough Council and recommend to Council that the
Monitoring Officer is delegated the authority to make the necessary
and consequential amendments to the Guildford Borough Council
Constitution’.
Reason(s):

1.      
Guildford
and Waverley Borough Councils have established several shared
services with executive functions, including a shared Legal
Service, Governance Team and Executive Support Team, as part of
their journey of collaborative working.

2.      
The
Governance model for such shared services is that Guildford Borough
Council has delegated the executive function for Waverley Borough
Council to carry out on their behalf.

3.      
To ensure
that Guildford Borough Council does not lose control of sovereignty
of decision making, it is important that all Executive decisions
relating to those shared services is undertaken by both
Councils’ Executives. Rather than duplicate the decision
making process, both Executives making collective decisions as part
of a joint committee is a governance arrangement that is agile,
quick, presents less risk and embraces collaborative
working.
Other options considered and rejected by the
Executive:
To
not establish a Joint Executive Committee with Waverley Borough
Council, leaving Waverley Borough Council to make decisions on
services being delivered by them on behalf of, or to, Guildford in
accordance with the delegated authority.
Details of any conflict of interest declared by the Leader or
lead councillors and any dispensation granted:
None.
topline: The Executive has decided to establish a Joint Executive Committee with Waverley Borough Council to oversee shared services and decision-making processes

content:
The Leader made the following
announcements.
 
Guildford Lido Open
Day
To celebrate the year-round
opening of Guildford Lido, visitors can enjoy a spectacular free
Open Day packed with swimming, workshops and fun for all
ages.  The event will run from 11am to
4pm on Saturday 18 October. You’ll need to 
book your place in advance on the Guildford Lido
website.
The Lido has now moved to its
new winter programme and will continue operating all year, with the
usual extended opening hours returning each summer.
 
Future vision for the Electric
Theatre to be explored with the community
We’ve begun exploring
options to secure the future of the much-loved Electric Theatre.
The community arts and theatre venue was handed back to the Council
by the previous leaseholder in August. We are organising a
roundtable discussion to bring interested parties together. This
will be an opportunity to explore ideas, share visions and help
shape a sustainable future for the Electric Theatre.
No decisions have been made at
this stage but those wishing to register their interest in the
future use of the Electric Theatre are invited to email AssetMan@guildford.gov.uk 
 
Street art transforms Old
Orleans building
We recently invited a group of
talented street artists to give the Old Orleans building a
makeover. It’s part of the next phase of our Street Art
Project, which looks to transform public spaces and use art to
create a greater sense of place and pride. 
We’re grateful to the
artists who donated their time and expertise free of
charge.
 
Cleaner Air Day is a
success
As part of our priority to make
Guildford a more sustainable borough, we held our second Cleaner
Air Day on Sunday 28 September. The High Street was filled with
live music, fun activities, market traders and delicious food
stalls. The day provided an opportunity for residents to better
understand the role they play in improving Guildford’s air
quality.
A big thank you to everyone who
worked hard to make this such a fantastic event!
